facts_of_case: Parties were married in 2015. A girl child was born in 2018 and is with the petitioner. The parties are living separately, and the petitioner works as a teacher in Jalandhar.

legal_principles.principle: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, 2022 SCC Online SC 1199

legal_principles.principle: When two or more proceedings are pending in different Courts between the same parties which raise common question of fact and law, and when the decisions in the cases are interdependent, it is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge.
legal_principles.held: It is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge so as to avoid multiplicity in trial of the same issues and conflict of decisions.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, 2022 SCC Online SC 1199
keywords: common question of fact and law

legal_principles.principle: While deciding the transfer application, the Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants.
legal_principles.held: The Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood.
cited_cases: Sumita Singh vs. Kumar Sanjay, AIR 2002 SC 396
Rajani Kishor Pardeshi vs. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) 12 SCC 237

legal_principles.principle: Transfer of legal proceedings from one Court to another should ordinarily be allowed, taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.
legal_principles.held: It is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge so as to avoid multiplicity in trial of the same issues and conflict of decisions.
cited_cases: Sumita Singh vs. Kumar Sanjay, AIR 2002 SC 396
Rajani Kishor Pardeshi vs. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) 12 SCC 237

outcome.final_order: The case was transferred to the Family Court at Jalandhar.
